# libarchive / libarchive_ar_fuzzer

libarchive's own fuzz target `libarchive_ar_fuzzer` ([source](source/libarchive_ar_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libarchive (libarchive/libarchive at 3670ecf7).

Reads the input as an ar archive (+ all filters); per entry calls pathname, size, mtime, mode, uid, gid and drains archive_read_data. Every return value is discarded.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libarchive at commit 3670ecf7.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libarchive` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `libarchive_ar_fuzzer.plain` | 810,384 | `798dd30c4b4727dcc94c1fe163be5a3cee2697ff046b087eadb99d97be7de6ed` |
| ubsan | `libarchive_ar_fuzzer.ubsan` | 823,440 | `08d9518b8d7cf9ad5f332022d95eb2899713f89649d63d03c9c20141211b0fdd` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libbz2.a` (a library from the build image), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `liblzma.a` (a library from the build image), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime), `libz.a` (a library from the build image), `libzstd.a` (a library from the build image)
